questions.q: According to this lesson, what do the six courses in the "Core Foundations" group (Data Governance Foundations through Data Security, Privacy & Classification) provide?
options: The vocabulary and fundamentals that every later course in the path assumed
Hands-on configuration steps for Microsoft Purview specifically
The career ladder from analyst to architect
A single certification exam covering the whole path
questions.explain: The lesson describes Core Foundations (Courses 1-6) as providing the vocabulary and fundamentals — governance basics, data quality, metadata/glossary, lineage, master data, and security/privacy/classification — that nothing afterward would make sense without.

questions.q: What distinguishes the "Platform Implementation" group of courses from the "Core Foundations" group, according to this lesson?
options: Platform Implementation makes the Core Foundations concepts concrete on real governance tools like Purview, Fabric, Unity Catalog, Snowflake, Power BI, and Azure/AWS governance services
Platform Implementation is entirely theoretical with no real tools involved
Platform Implementation came before Core Foundations in the path
There is no meaningful difference between the two groups
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly describes Platform Implementation (Courses 7-12) as turning the conceptual understanding from Core Foundations into concrete configuration on real platforms.

questions.q: Which three courses make up the "Advanced & Specialized Governance" group in this path, according to this lesson?
options: AI & Machine Learning Governance, Data Governance Program Management, and Data Governance Architecture
Data Quality Management, Metadata Management & Business Glossary, and Data Lineage & Impact Analysis
Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Fabric Data Governance, and Snowflake Data Governance
Power BI Governance, Cloud Data Governance: Azure & AWS, and Data Governance Career & Capstone
questions.explain: The lesson groups AI & Machine Learning Governance, Data Governance Program Management, and Data Governance Architecture together as the path's most senior, specialized territory, directly connecting to the career ladder from Lesson 34.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say there is no "next lesson" or "next course" pointed to from here?
options: Because this is the final lesson of the entire 16-course Data Governance career path, not a pause within it
Because the course was cancelled before completion
Because the next course has not been written yet but will be added later
Because the learner failed to meet a prerequisite for a next course
questions.explain: This lesson is explicit that it is the end of the entire path, not an incomplete stopping point — there genuinely is no next course in this catalog's Data Governance path.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what are some valid honest directions after finishing the path (without ranking them as mandatory)?
options: Using the capstone in real job applications, deepening on a specific platform, pursuing a certification that fits a direction already chosen, or simply starting the work
Immediately retaking all sixteen courses from the beginning
Waiting indefinitely until a seventeenth course is published
Avoiding any application to real jobs until every possible certification is completed first
questions.explain: The lesson lists several equally valid directions — applying to jobs, deepening a platform specialty, pursuing a certification that fits, or simply starting the work — none of which are presented as required before the other.
